rationale: GEO holds three screens from the paper's Cebpb arm (Supplementary Data 11-12): a genome-wide screen in Cebpb-KO DCs and a 661-gene secondary library (Cebpb-regulated genes, 10 guides per gene, 6,513 guides, no non-targeting guides) screened in Cebpb-KO and in Cebpb-WT DCs, each sorted into the top and bottom 10% of CD86 with one library per bin. The paper's MAGeCK compares Low with High (Cd86 is the top positive gene), so every analysis is CD86-low versus CD86-high; a gene enriched in the low bin is a positive regulator of CD86. The record's primary analysis is the Cebpb-KO secondary screen, the one the paper uses to show that Nr4a3 mediates the CD86 increase of Cebpb-targeted cells; the WT secondary (design_wt.json) and the genome-wide Cebpb-KO screen (design_gw.json) are run alongside. One library per bin: no-replicate path with overdispersion pooled over all guides (no controls), so calls are screening-level and calibration could not be checked. The paper's main WT genome-wide and secondary CD86/PD-L1 screens (Chd4, Stat5b, Egr2, Med12) are deposited in other series, not here.
